'''Virginia Vassilevska Williams''' (née Virginia Panayotova Vassilevska){{r|cv}} is a theoretical computer scientist and mathematician known for her research in [[computational complexity theory]] and [[algorithms]]. She is currently the Steven and Renee Finn Career Development Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].{{r|sloan}} She is notable for her breakthrough results in [[Coppersmith–Winograd algorithm|fast matrix multiplication]],{{r|stoc}} for her work on [[Dynamic problem (algorithms)|dynamic algorithms]],{{r|dynamiclowerbounds}} and for helping to develop the field of [[Fine-grained reduction|fine-grained complexity]].{{r|finegrained}}

==Education and career==
Williams is originally from [[Bulgaria]], and attended a German-language high school in [[Sofia]].{{r|true}} She graduated from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 2003, and completed her Ph.D. at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 2008.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Efficient Algorithms for Path Problems in Weighted Graphs'', was supervised by [[Guy Blelloch]].{{r|mgp}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and [[University of California, Berkeley]], Williams became an assistant professor of computer science at [[Stanford University]] in 2013.{{r|cv}} She moved to MIT as an associate professor in 2017.{{r|sloan}}

==Research==
In 2011, Williams found an algorithm for multiplying two <math>n\times n</math> matrices in time <math>O(n^{2.373})</math>. This improved a previous time bound for [[matrix multiplication algorithm]]s, the [[Coppersmith–Winograd algorithm]], that had stood as the best known for 24 years. Her initial improvement was independent of Andrew Stothers, who also improved the same bound a year earlier; after learning of Stothers' work, she combined ideas from both methods to improve his bound as well.{{r|ns|stoc}} With collaborators, in 2023 she extended this bound to  <math>O(n^{2.371552})</math> {{r|matrix2023}}{{r|quanta2024}}, and later in 2024 to <math>O(n^{2.371339})</math>.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Alman |first1=Josh |title=More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication |date=2024-10-20 |eprint=2404.16349 |last2=Duan |first2=Ran |last3=Williams |first3=Virginia Vassilevska |last4=Xu |first4=Yinzhan |last5=Xu |first5=Zixuan |last6=Zhou |first6=Renfei |class=cs.DS }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Williams was an NSF Computing Innovation Fellow for 2009–2011,{{r|cv}} and won a Sloan Research Fellowship in 2017.{{r|sloan}} She was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on Mathematical Aspects of Computer Science.{{r|icm}}

==Personal life==
Williams is the daughter of applied mathematicians Panayot Vassilevski and Tanya Kostova-Vassilevska.{{r|engage}} She is married to [[Ryan Williams (computer scientist)|Ryan Williams]], also a computer science professor at MIT; they have worked together in the field of [[Fine-grained reduction|fine-grained complexity]].{{r|true}}
